security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown formatting, documentation links, or metadata URLs and are false positives. No prompt-injection text, credential exfiltration, or hidden network behavior was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Quote artifact and aggregate identifier values, or show an argument-array invocation so user-provided values cannot be parsed as shell syntax.

remediation.suggestion: Provide a small trusted wrapper that resolves the repository root and validates it before invoking registry scripts.

content.value_statement: Project context becomes stale, duplicated, and difficult to retrieve across sessions. This skill organizes authorized working memory while preserving canonical records and privacy controls.
actual_capabilities: Initialize private HOT, WARM, and COLD memory from repository templates after authorization.
Review project priorities, evidence pointers, and registry offsets without changing canonical facts.
Consolidate duplicate non-canonical notes while preserving conflicts and source provenance.
Archive stale HOT and WARM notes with metadata that preserves traceability.
Plan and execute authorized working-memory erasure with scope reporting and minimal tombstones.
Create session checkpoints and pointer-only audit indexes for approved workflows.
limitations: It does not accept registry proposals or change canonical registry facts.
Persistent writes and erasure actions require explicit authorization.
It cannot guarantee removal from Git history, backups, or external systems.
It relies on valid project-local templates, registry tools, and access permissions.

use_cases.title: Resume a project safely
use_cases.description: Review current priorities and evidence pointers before continuing work in a new session.

use_cases.title: Consolidate research notes
use_cases.description: Merge equivalent working notes while retaining conflicts, provenance, and registry ownership boundaries.

use_cases.title: Handle an erasure request
use_cases.description: Prepare an authorized working-memory purge with precise scope and honest retention limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize private project memory from the available templates. Show the planned paths and ask for authorization before writing.

prompt_templates.title: Review current context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current HOT and WARM memory. List priorities, open loops, source pointers, and any stale entries. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify duplicate non-canonical notes for this project. Propose a consolidation plan that preserves conflicts and provenance. Wait for approval before writing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan privacy erasure
prompt_templates.scenario: Respond to an authorized data request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dry-run erasure plan for the pseudonymous subject ID [ID]. Show affected working-memory paths, required authorization, retention limits, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Review current project memory without making changes.
output: Current priority: complete the campaign brief.
Evidence pointer: WARM research note dated 2026-07-10.
Open loop: confirm consent status before outreach.

output_examples.input: Archive stale WARM notes after approval.
output: Archived three notes older than 90 days.
Each archive retains its source pointer, content hash, and original path.
Registry projections and event streams were not changed.

output_examples.input: Prepare an erasure dry run for Subject-A1B2.
output: Found four working-memory paths requiring review.
No deletion was performed during the dry run.
Git history and backups require a separate retention procedure.

best_practices: Use read-only review or a dry run before any persistent memory operation.
Record source dates, authorization references, and registry offsets with each durable note.
Keep personal data and credentials out of templates, HOT summaries, and event payloads.
anti_patterns: Do not treat cached memory as proof of current consent or canonical truth.
Do not merge conflicting evidence without preserving the conflict and its provenance.
Do not claim that a working-tree purge erases Git history, backups, or external records.

faq.question: Does this skill change canonical registry facts?
faq.answer: No. It creates proposals for registry-owned facts and leaves acceptance to the authorized registry owner.

faq.question: When does the skill ask for permission?
faq.answer: It asks before persistent writes unless the current request explicitly authorizes the named operation.

faq.question: What are HOT, WARM, and COLD memory?
faq.answer: They are working-memory layers for current summaries, evidence artifacts, and historical notes.

faq.question: Can it remove personal data?
faq.answer: It can handle authorized working-memory erasure, but it cannot guarantee removal from history, backups, or external systems.

faq.question: Can it use old notes as current facts?
faq.answer: No. It labels stale data and requires live registry or consent checks when current truth is needed.

faq.question: Is it suitable for cross-session handoffs?
faq.answer: Yes. It maintains bounded checkpoints and evidence pointers for safe session resumption.
